article.headline: Scores from last Night: Tupelo rolls on; South Panola ends Lake Cormorant’s perfect run
article.html:
Tupelo stayed unbeaten, Germantown survived overtime at Oxford, and South Panola ended Lake Cormorant’s perfect season Friday as Mississippi’s football playoffs moved closer to the state championships. The Golden Wave won 42–7, the Mavericks escaped 49–42, and the Tigers advanced with a 16–14 road victory.

Those postseason results lead this November 20, 2026, selection, which also includes basketball doubleheaders and soccer finals. Records below are postgame figures listed on the completed matchup reports. Unreported or conflicting results are excluded rather than treated as completed games.

Tupelo and Germantown set up North championship meeting

Tupelo beat Madison Central 42–7 and reached 13–0, ending the Jaguars’ season at a listed 7–5. The Golden Wave scored 14 points in each of the first three quarters. Madison Central scored in the opening quarter but was held scoreless for the rest of the game, allowing Tupelo to keep extending its lead.

Germantown’s route was much tighter. The Mavericks won 49–42 in overtime at Oxford to improve to 8–4; Oxford finished at 9–3. Germantown outscored the Chargers 14–7 in the fourth quarter, then posted a 7–0 overtime period to settle a game that had stayed close through regulation.

The MHSAA-linked Class 7A bracket now pairs Germantown at Tupelo in the North championship and Brandon at Oak Grove in the South championship. Both are listed for November 27. Friday’s winners are one victory away from reaching the state final.

South Panola ends Lake Cormorant’s unbeaten run

South Panola edged Lake Cormorant 16–14 in the Class 6A second round, leaving the Gators at 11–1 and moving the Tigers to a listed 7–4. South Panola scored six points in the second quarter, seven in the third and three in the fourth. Lake Cormorant scored seven in each of the final two quarters, but could not erase the deficit.

The Tigers next face unbeaten Warren Central, which defeated Canton 42–24 to reach 12–0. Canton finished at 9–3. The bracket lists South Panola at Warren Central for the North championship on November 27, giving the Tigers another unbeaten opponent after their breakthrough at Lake Cormorant.

Oak Grove and Brandon advance in Class 7A

Oak Grove beat D’Iberville 35–7 and is listed at 10–2; D’Iberville also finished at 10–2. Oak Grove scored 14 in the first quarter and 21 in the second, while holding the visitors scoreless until the fourth. Its strong first half made the rest of the night about protecting a commanding advantage.

Brandon won 39–21 at Meridian to reach 9–3, with the Wildcats finishing 8–4. The Bulldogs outscored Meridian 17–0 in the second quarter and held the hosts scoreless again in the third. The result earned Brandon the trip to Oak Grove with the South championship at stake.

Picayune rallies; Hattiesburg stays alive

Picayune defeated West Jones 34–24 after being outscored in both opening quarters. The Maroon Tide won the third quarter 14–0 and the fourth 17–14, turning the game around after halftime. Picayune is listed at 9–3 and West Jones at 9–4.

Hattiesburg beat Hancock 35–10 to reach a listed 9–3, ending the Hawks’ season at 7–5. The Tigers will visit Picayune in the Class 6A South championship November 27, according to the MHSAA-linked bracket.

More playoff finals: close escapes and perfect records

Calhoun City held off Tupelo Christian Prep 34–32, handing the Eagles their first loss and leaving them at 11–1. Calhoun City is listed at 8–3. TCP outscored the Wildcats 13–0 in the fourth quarter, but its late push came up short.

Noxubee County survived Choctaw County 14–13 to reach 11–2. The teams each scored seven in the second quarter; Noxubee County scored seven in the fourth to Choctaw County’s six. The Chargers finished at a listed 5–7.

West Point won 35–28 at Cleveland Central, keeping its postseason alive at a listed 5–7 while Cleveland Central finished 8–4. Louisville beat Shannon 43–16; the Wildcats are 11–2 and the Red Raiders 10–3.

Brookhaven and Poplarville both protected perfect records. Brookhaven beat Laurel 51–6 to reach 12–0, with Laurel at 5–7. Poplarville won 27–6 at Greene County and also is listed at 12–0; the Wildcats finished 9–4.

Basketball: Biggersville and North Pontotoc split

North Pontotoc’s girls beat Biggersville 54–49 to reach 7–2, handing the Lions their first loss at 4–1. Biggersville’s boys answered with a 56–54 victory and are listed at 1–1; North Pontotoc’s boys are 6–2.

Walnut swept Strayhorn, winning the girls’ game 64–14 and the boys’ game 64–49. The Wildcats’ girls are listed at 7–1 and their boys at 4–1. In the boys’ game, Walnut jumped ahead with a 23–4 first quarter, giving the hosts an early cushion.

Booneville also swept, beating Ridgeland 55–42 in girls basketball and 75–63 in boys basketball. The completed reports list the Blue Devil girls at 2–0 and boys at 1–0; Ridgeland’s corresponding records are 3–3 and 3–4.

Wheeler won 66–59 at Alcorn Central in boys basketball. The Eagles are listed at 4–1 following the road victory, while Alcorn Central is 1–3.

Soccer: DeSoto Central sweeps; Center Hill splits

DeSoto Central edged Olive Branch 4–3 in girls soccer and won the boys’ match 2–0. The Jaguars’ girls are listed at 2–4 and boys at 5–1–1. Olive Branch’s postgame records are 4–2 for the girls and 2–5 for the boys.

Florence won the girls’ match at Center Hill 2–1, but the Mustangs took the boys’ match 1–0. Florence’s girls are listed at 5–3 and Center Hill’s at 2–5. Both boys teams are 5–3 after the split.

For earlier postseason coverage, see our earlier first-round recap. This is a selected report of verified finals, not a complete statewide scoreboard; results from other sports were not included where full event-date and final-result evidence was unavailable.
